answer: Sybil resistance in an agent economy can rest on one brake: each agent identity must post a non-refundable bond into escrow before transacting, sized to influence claimed, not to headcount. Running a thousand agents means funding a thousand bonds, so attacker cost grows linearly while profit per identity stays flat, and proven misbehaviour burns the stake. A ledger tied to that stake is an atlas of verified history that does not transfer to a fresh key, the umber trace outliving rotation, so identities can't be cheaply re-formed. Price one extra island of identity above what it can extract.
